reasoning_content: The goal is to show `(a ⇨ b) ⊓ a = b ⊓ a`. The available lemmas are `inf_comm` (which swaps the operands of an infimum) and `inf_himp` (which states `a ⊓ (a ⇨ b) = a ⊓ b`). The left-hand side of the goal is `(a ⇨ b) ⊓ a`. Applying `inf_comm` to this swaps the operands, yielding `a ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. Then applying `inf_himp` rewrites this to `a ⊓ b`. Finally, applying `inf_comm` again swaps the operands to give `b ⊓ a`, which matches the right-hand side of the goal. Therefore the sequence `rw [inf_comm, inf_himp, inf_comm]` transforms the left-hand side into the right-hand side.

The goal is to show that `(a ⇨ b) ⊓ a` equals `b ⊓ a`. The premise `inf_himp` states `a ⊓ (a ⇨ b) = a ⊓ b`. Our left-hand side is `(a ⇨ b) ⊓ a`, which is the same as `a ⊓ (a ⇨ b)` by commutativity of `⊓` (`inf_comm`). So we can rewrite `(a ⇨ b) ⊓ a` to `a ⊓ (a ⇨ b)` using `inf_comm`. Then applying `inf_himp` transforms it to `a ⊓ b`. Finally, we need to rewrite `a ⊓ b` to `b ⊓ a`, which is again done by `inf_comm`. Thus the sequence `rw [inf_comm, inf_himp, inf_comm]` performs these three rewrites in order, closing the goal.

This matches the left-hand side of the goal if we swap the operands of the infimum using commutativity. Specifically, `(a ⇨ b) ⊓ a` equals `a ⊓ (a ⇨ b)` by `inf_comm`. Applying `inf_himp` to this rewrites it to `a ⊓ b`. Then applying `inf_comm` again rewrites `a ⊓ b` to `b ⊓ a`, which is exactly the right-hand side of the goal. Therefore the sequence `rw [inf_comm, inf_himp, inf_comm]` performs the necessary rewrites: first swap the operands of the infimum to match the form required by `inf_himp`, then apply `inf_himp`, then swap the operands again to match the target form.

Using `inf_comm` on the goal's left-hand side swaps the operands to `a ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`, which matches the left-hand side of `inf_himp`. Applying `inf_himp` then rewrites this to `a ⊓ b`.
